articles.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Hard Mode Is No Joke — Watch AI-Controlled Orks Wipe the Floor With 2 Developers Playing Space Marines
articles.summary: When developers show off their games, they tend to defeat the enemy AI in spectacular fashion. But that’s exactly the opposite of what happens in the gameplay King Art Games just released for its upcoming real-time strategy game Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4.
body: In the video, below, creative director Jan Theysen and senior game designer Elliott Verbiest team up against Hard AI Orks in a 2v2 Team Skirmish PvE battle. These two developers have been at the helm of pretty much all the Dawn of War 4 battlefield report videos released so far. But those previous gameplay videos focus on PvP; this time, Theysen and Verbiest join forces to face the enemy AI — and they decide to go up against hard mode.

The video shows two matches, the first of which goes so spectacularly badly for the poor developers that they suffer defeat in just over four minutes. They declare that a practice round — mere training before the second match, in which the pair promise they're “locked in.” They also increase the number of Victory Points needed to help extend the length of the match... just in case.
points: When developers show off their games, they tend to defeat the enemy AI in spectacular fashion.
But that’s exactly the opposite of what happens in the gameplay King Art Games just released for its upcoming real-time strategy game Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4.

articles.title: Meta Connect 2026 Live Blog – What's Next for VR?
articles.summary: Just a week after the Steam Frame presented Valve's vision for VR gaming, Meta is getting ready to take the stage at Meta Connect 2026. While I don't imagine the Meta Quest 4 will be headlining, there have been a ton of rumors swirling around about its XR 'Phoenix' headset.
body: I'd love to see Meta at least tease a Meta Quest 4. Its current-generation Meta Quest 3 headset is still one of the most cost-effective ways to get into VR. However, because the Quest 3 and 3S haven't gone up in price, it's possible that Meta will avoid even mentioning a next-generation version, due to the cost increases it'd likely have to bear.

If you'd like to watch Meta Connect 2026 keynote yourself, it will be streamed on Meta's website, or on Facebook at 4pm PDT / 7pm EDT on September 29. I will be updating this article live, so if you won't want to watch Zuckerberg talk about AI for an hour, you can just stay tuned here, and I'll do it for you.

6:00pm: If the leaks and rumors are to be believed, the headline device this year is going to be a sort of VR headset, but instead of it being closed off like the Steam Frame or the Meta Quest 3, it'll be worn similarly to regular glasses, but with traditional VR optics built into them. If that's true, I have serious doubts about how Meta would stop light from leaking in.

articles.title: Discord Begins Rolling Out Age Verification–And A Sponsorship With FanDuel
articles.summary: Discord has officially begun rolling out age-verification measures as of today. The company first announced age verification--and, subsequently, limits placed on accounts of those under 18-- back in February of this year, but delayed a full implementation until just recently.
body: While Discord assures users that "More than 90% of you won’t be asked to confirm your age," the company also acknowledge that their model isn't flawless, and some accounts will need to verify their age to use a non-age-restricted Discord account. If users want to avoid uploading ID or video, they can use services like Apple Pay, Google Play, Google Wallet, or AgeKey, or enter a credit card number.

With any attempt at age verification comes controversy, however, and users of Discord were quick to notice that age verification was rolling out at the exact same time as sponsored ads for sports betting website FanDuel were appearing for American users. Obviously, it's illegal to use FanDuel if you're under 21 (or 18 in some jurisdictions), so it didn't take much for social media users to assume a connection between the two events.

articles.title: Producer of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Movie Reportedly Working on New Silent Hill Film
articles.summary: A new report from The Wall Street Journal states that Roy Lee, who produced Zach Cregger’s hugely-successful Resident Evil movie, is now working on a Silent Hill film. Roy Lee is a Hollywood legend.
body: Roy Lee is a Hollywood legend. The producer has had a hand in some of the most successful movies of the last three decades and has a speciality for adapting pre-existing IP, specifically where horror is concerned.

He began his career with horror hits like The Grudge and The Ring, and went on to produce Zach Cregger’s Barbarian and Weapons 20 years later. Most recently, he helped bring Cregger’s Resident Evil to life, which has become the single most-successful film adaptation of Capcom’s video game series ever and the highest-rated video game movie of all time.
Now, it seems that he’s working on yet another iconic survival horror franchise: Silent Hill.
The Wall Street Journal published a feature about Roy Lee on September 20, where the outlet shed some light on the producer’s upcoming video game-related projects.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Reacts to Fans Asking for Him to Play the Joker After Primetime Performance Goes Viral
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson’s captivating performance as Chris Hansen in A24’s Primetime has sparked an unexpected trend; fans are now wondering what Pattinson’s take on the Joker would look like. The actor’s portrayal of Hansen has received acclaim from both critics and casual audiences alike.
body: One of his lines from the movie’s trailers has already become a viral meme (“You see how this looks, right?”), and fans just can’t get enough of his chilling stare and near-sociopathic take on Hansen, prompting them to ask the question: “What if he played the Joker?”

In the lead-up to Primetime’s release on September 25, curious Batman fans are hypothetically casting him in James Gunn’s separate DC cinematic universe, wondering what his Hansen-esque Joker would look like, were he able and willing to play the part.
“Really sucks he’s Batman, ‘cause his Joker would’ve been generational,” one fan wrote in a post on X.
“F**k it, let Robert Pattinson play Joker and Batman,” another said, while another mused that the “only bad part about Robert Pattinson being such a good Batman is that he’d make such a good Joker.”

articles.title: Rainbow Six Siege Dev On Competing With GTA 6 And Why There Are No Plans For Siege 2
articles.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 releases this November, and it's expected to take up a lot of time and attention, leading some to worry how other games may fare in its wake.
body: "All of us are going to play it," Mills told The Game Business.

So what can Ubisoft do for Siege when GTA 6 comes out? He said, "It's about being smart and with your expectations so you can keep the team and HQ aligned." He said if the developers working on Siege see the game's player numbers drop, "they can get anxious." However, he observed that the effect on player numbers from a big competitor release is "generally temporary."
Whatever the case, Mills said the "golden rule" that Ubisoft operates by is by serving "the players who stay like kings and queens."
"We don’t go on vacation just because a competitor is swelling the market. We double down and reward those spending their valuable time with us," he said.

articles.title: 30 Years Later, Collecting Pokemon Cards Hits A Little Different
articles.summary: Let me sound like an old for a second. I remember in the late '90s and early '00s, collecting Pokemon cards was a casual hobby. You'd go to your local brick-and-mortar store with the money you made from mowing the lawn or whatever, drop maybe $10 on a couple of packs, rip them open, then go to your…
body: It was so low-key back in the day. Saying that grosses me out, as I sound like a Boomer or Gen Xer, but it's true: Collecting Pokemon cards wasn't that serious, and we didn't put much stock in the cards, stuffing them in bags or pockets and watching them turn up in washing machines.

There have been plenty of incidents involving card collecting and violence lately. Robbers stole over $100,000 in rare cards from a California store in December 2025. A different set of robbers made off with nearly $120,000 in rare cards at gunpoint in New York in January 2026. Police broke up a chaotic Costco scene over Prismatic Evolutions in April 2026. And more recently, a Connecticut man was arrested for assaulting someone in a Target after being confronted for exceeding the store's limit for Pokemon card packs, while a 72-year-old Ohio man pleaded guilty to using a GPS tracker to stalk a woman stocking Pokemon cards.

articles.title: All paralogue dates and deadlines in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
articles.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's paralogues operate on strict deadlines, and they can be very easy to miss. However, they're among the most important optional quests you can take on.
body: Below, we list all paralogues in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave and explain how they work and when you may — or may not — want to complete them.

The answer to that question depends on whose path you're playing, who you want in the endgame, whether you have time for multiple paths — or just how broke you are. Paralogues reward you with 20,000 gold each, so if you've spent all your gold bribing people with food and gift items, they're a solid way to get some cash back in your pocket.

Anyway, here's how Fortune's Weave 's paralogues work. Every Flame Lord, including the non-playable ones (that's Bertrand, Anatolia, Talimun, and Orchel), has a paralogue, and Anna does as well. Completing a Flame Lord's paralogue ensures they join your team in Part 3, though there is a caveat to note here. If you complete Leda's, Dietrich's, Cai's, or Theodora's paralogues, they join in Part 3 as guests only. You have no control over their class, leveling, or inventory. When you complete Talimun's, Orchel's, Bertrand's, or Anatolia's paralogues, they join in Part 3 as full-fledged members whose classes you can change and so on, not just as guests.
points: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's paralogues operate on strict deadlines, and they can be very easy to miss.
However, they're among the most important optional quests you can take on.

articles.title: High On Life Is Helping Make The Case For Bigger Games On Quest
articles.summary: High on Life has been a big hit since it first launched in 2022, thanks to its bizarre sense of humor, motor-mouthed guns, and polished gameplay. But can it succeed as a virtual reality port?
body: While it's still early days for the project, I took the time to chat to High on Life VR game director Emily O'Neal and Eric Masher, co-founder and chief operating officer for Impact Reality and Flat2VR Studios, about this project and the challenges involved in adapting it for a new platform.

"We want to bring them those high-quality games like High on Life, that [have] more teeth, more depth, and more playability as an actual game. We're not here just for a short snapshot in time; we're here to help grow this industry to where it will be in three to five years from now. Our job and our mission at Flat2VR is to bring the immersive, amazing games that you love playing right now on your console and PC, but bring it to another platform that makes a whole bunch of sense and that feels completely different but still the same.”

Bringing High on Life to VR isn't an easy task either, as you can't just press a "Convert to VR" button for a project of this scale. As O'Neal explained, the original game is massive, and the team is looking to make it run as smoothly as possible on a VR headset.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Would Never Work on PS5 or Xbox
articles.summary: After playing the Forever beta using a gamepad, I think I know why. It's not that the gamepad support is bad — it's actually very good. It's a totally viable way to play the game. But you would never mistake it for a game that was meant to be played this way.
body: At BlizzCon, the developers of World of Warcraft: Forever — Blizzard's new, remixed and updated version of classic WoW — told Polygon that although Forever finally brings official gamepad support to WoW, that doesn't mean the MMO is coming to consoles. Which, on the face of it, is a bit odd. WoW either works to Blizzard's satisfaction on a gamepad, or it doesn't. If it does, why wouldn't Blizzard take the opportunity to bring one of the most-played games of all time to a whole new audience?

When it comes to playing WoW on a gamepad, I have biases that cut both ways. I generally prefer to play games with a controller and not at my desk. But World of Warcraft is the exception. I have been playing for 21 years and counting, and the mouse-and-keyboard controls are hardwired into my muscle memory. I can't even deal with switching away from the old-school WASD map — where A and D turn your character, rather than strafe — to the modern setup. I have autorun and movement skills mapped just where I want them on my mouse buttons. It's so comfortable. After so many hundreds — thousands? — of hours, why would I change?
points: After playing the Forever beta using a gamepad, I think I know why.
It's not that the gamepad support is bad — it's actually very good.
But you would never mistake it for a game that was meant to be played this way.

articles.title: Hackers Behind Flopped 'GTA 6' Leak Officially Threatening the FBI Now
articles.summary: ShinyHunters, the hacking group that went viral in April after threatening Grand Theft Auto 6 developer Rockstar Games with a leak, is back with a much more dangerous scheme. This time, the group is brazenly going after the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation.
body: The numbers were interesting to groups like journalists and analysts — companies like Rockstar might share financial data during investor calls, but those disclosures are broad. Knowing that GTA Online makes around $1 million a day is slightly shocking in that context. For most people, though, ShinyHunter's leak was a big nothingburger.

Incidentally, the FBI issued a public service announcement about the ShinyHunters group a month before the hackers went after Rockstar. The prolific group had grown in notoriety after breaching institutions like Harvard University and Pornhub, and the high-profile security leaks were emboldening them to take on bigger targets. At the time, the FBI accused ShinyHunters of using "harassment strategies, sending threatening text messages and phone calls to victims and their family members, and in some cases, swatting."

According to the New York Times, ShinyHunters took umbrage with that description. The group tried to retaliate against the FBI by stealing current and former employee information. The data was sourced from an online job portal, meaning that ShinyHunters also had access to intelligence on people who have applied to work at the FBI.

articles.title: Discord launches controversial age-verification system "using the most privacy-preserving approach we could build" months after first delay
articles.summary: Discord delayed the rollout of its controversial age verification system back in February after very loud backlash against the company's plans. Those age checks are now back, but this time, co-founder and chief technology officer Stanislav Vishnevskiy says the updated system will give users options…
body: Near the start of the year, Discord's age checks planned to automatically give all users a "teen-appropriate experience" by blurring potentially "sensitive content" or restricting access to age-gated channels. Getting rid of the blocks would have required users to verify their age by submitting a photo of their government-issued ID or a video recording of their face to one of the platform's third-party vendors. As you can imagine, Discord users weren't thrilled about sharing sensitive data like that.

"Age assurance draws strong opinions and scepticism, especially when it involves sharing biometric information or a form of ID," Vishnevskiy said in a new blog post. "At the same time, age assurance laws are expanding, and since my last post we've had to launch age assurance in other regions, including in Brazil and in Texas. We're hearing from policymakers in countless states and countries who want stronger teen protections, from the European Union to Indonesia. To me, that makes it more important than ever to show that this can be done in a privacy-preserving way: one where more than 90% of you won’t have to confirm your age."

articles.title: All classes and unlock requirements in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
articles.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave classes work a bit differently than you might be used to if you played Three Houses. They come in several tiers, similar to Three Houses, but some of the intermediate classes only unlock if you meet certain conditions.
body: Below, we list Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's classes and how to unlock them, including Divine classes.

Every character starts in a beginner class, either commoner or noble, and gets a helpful little class mastery skill. After that, it's time to change to something more specialized. A new tier of classes unlocks when you reach certain renown thresholds, and you'll need to purchase certifications to take that class' exam. The game autosaves before you see the exam result, so there's no chance of cheesing it and retaking the exam until you pass.

The better option is to just hold off taking an exam until your character has at least a 75% chance of passing or higher. Skill rank matters here, but level matters even more. If you need to be level 35, for example, but you take the exam at level 32 with the right skill ranks, you'll still end up with a low chance of passing.
points: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave classes work a bit differently than you might be used to if you played Three Houses.
They come in several tiers, similar to Three Houses, but some of the intermediate classes only unlock if you meet certain conditions.

articles.title: As Halo goes to Activision, fans are worried about this year's Halo Fest and a potential lore reboot from the Call of Duty publisher
articles.summary: We're now living in a timeline that would have been impossible to comprehend for a grunt-squashing teen in 2007: Activision is making the next Halo game. And, now, fans have questions about the change. Is this year's Halo Fest still happening, despite sweeping layoffs at Halo Studios?
body: "We are eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the XGS management and central functions layer," Xbox Studios chief Matt Booty wrote in a statement this week as part of the console maker's wide-ranging restructure. "Activision will also be developing the next Halo title, led by a new, purpose-built team that is separate from ongoing development and plans for Call of Duty. A small team at Halo Studios will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market."

Xbox's restructuring laid off 1,600 workers this summer, with a further 1,600 job cuts planned over the course of the year, but it also rejigged several studios. Obsidian is now part of Bethesda, for example, and Halo is now part of Activision, along with Rare and World's Edge.

It's a dramatic shift for a franchise that was once Xbox's golden goose, and fans are conflicted about what it means for the future of the iconic sci-fi shooter series. One big worry is Activision may reboot the story and throw away lore that's been built up across 25 years - or, perhaps, scrap some of the extended universe lore, as Disney did to Star Wars when it took over that galaxy.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever's first patch will bring back the number one thing seasoned players missed from the MMO's past: storms
articles.summary: If there's one thing that Blizzard nailed with World of Warcraft: Forever, it's the atmosphere. There's nothing quite like walking under the moonlight in Tirisfal Glades listening to distant howls and flapping wings on the way to your next quest.
body: "I miss running through Dun Morogh hearing the iconic music with a massive snowstorm lowering my view distance on my Dwarf hunter, picking up quests from the dwarf next to the fire [and] restoring my inventory," Reddit user Darthbobz wrote in a post pleading Blizzard to bring WoW's old weather effects to WoW: Forever.

It's not that it doesn't rain or snow in WoW: Forever, it's that it doesn't rain and snow enough. People like Darthbobz want to be blinded by the amount of weather on screen, not surrounded by the suggestion of a storm.

Blizzard even says the core pillars of WoW: Forever are that the world is the main character and that the journey is more important than the destination. For the most part that's true: Over half of the experience involves running around forests and deserts rather than flying across them on a mount like you do in the modern version of the MMO. But the diet weather effects in the beta clash with the rest of Blizzard's commitment to adding friction back into the MMO.

Note: Stellar Blade's developer has now confirmed that a frame-gen toggle will be added:
Stellar Blade on Switch 2 uses frame generation to target 60fps - and Capcom is offering the same feature with a toggle in the upcoming Dragon's Dogma 2 port.
Beyond that, Tom, Rich and Oliver discuss whether next-gen hardware should be delayed, why Nintendo is avoiding DLSS in its own Switch 2 titles and whether Valve should release an ARM-based handheld.
